title: Java Tutorial
description: Master Java step-by-step, from installation to advanced OOP concepts. Includes interactive code challenges and practical examples for each topic.

content.content: Install Java (JDK)
Download and install the JDK (Java Development Kit) from the official website. After installation, verify in your terminal:

java -version
javac -version
Your First Compile & Run
Basic Program Structure
Every Java app starts from the main method inside a class. Class name should match filename.

questions.question: Print 'Hello, Java!'

content.content: Printing in Java
Use System.out.println for line output and System.out.print to continue on the same line.

questions.question: Print exactly: Welcome to Java!

content.content: Single-line & Multi-line
Use // for single-line comments and /* ... */ for multi-line comments.

questions.question: Write a single-line comment 'My first Java program' and print Hello

content.content: Declaring Variables
Java is statically typed. You must declare a type before using a variable.

questions.question: Create an int x = 10 and print it

content.content: Primitive Types
Common primitives: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, boolean.

questions.question: Declare a double price = 9.99 and print it

content.content: Widening & Narrowing
Widening happens automatically; narrowing requires explicit cast.

questions.question: Cast 7.8 to int and print it

content.content: Arithmetic, Relational, Logical
Use + - * / % for arithmetic; == != > < >= <= for comparison; && || ! for logic.

questions.question: Add 12 and 13 and print the result

content.content: Working with Strings
Strings are objects. Common methods: length(), substring(), toUpperCase(), toLowerCase(), contains().

questions.question: Store 'Java' and print the first 2 letters

content.content: Math Utilities
Use Math.max, Math.min, Math.sqrt, Math.abs, Math.random, etc.

System.out.println(Math.max(5, 9));
System.out.println(Math.sqrt(16));

questions.question: Print the square root of 49

content.content: True/False
Booleans hold true or false. Often used in conditions.

boolean ok = (10 > 5);
System.out.println(ok);

questions.question: Print the result of (7 > 3)

content.content: Conditional Branching
Use if, else if, and else to branch logic.

questions.question: If 5 < 10 print Yes

content.content: Switch Statement
Switch selects a branch based on matching case value.

questions.question: Using switch, print 'Three' when x = 3

content.content: While Loop
Repeats while a condition remains true. Be careful to update the loop variable.

questions.question: Print numbers 1 to 3 using while

content.content: For Loop
Compact loop with initializer; condition; increment.

questions.question: Print 0, 1, 2 each on new line using for

content.content: Controlling Loop Flow
break exits a loop; continue skips to the next iteration.

questions.question: Print 1 and 3 (skipping 2) using continue

content.content: Array Basics
Arrays store fixed-size sequences of elements of the same type.

int[] nums = {1, 2, 3};
System.out.println(nums[1]);

questions.question: Create int[] a = {2,4,6} and print the last element

content.content: Defining & Calling Methods
Methods group reusable code. static methods can be called without creating objects.

questions.question: Write a method greet() that prints Hello and call it once

content.content: Passing Arguments
Parameters let you pass data into methods.

questions.question: Create a method add(int a, int b) and print sum of 2 and 5

content.content: Same Name, Different Params
Overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists.

static int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
static double add(double a, double b) { return a + b; }

questions.question: Overload sum so it works for (2,3) and (2.5,3.5). Print both results

content.content: Local vs Class Scope
Variables defined inside methods are local; fields belong to the class instance.

questions.question: Inside a method, declare int temp = 42 and print it

content.content: Functions Calling Themselves
Recursion solves a problem by calling the same method with smaller inputs.

questions.question: Write a recursive method to compute factorial(3) and print result

content.content: Defining a Class
Classes define blueprints for objects (fields + methods).

questions.question: Create a class Person with a String name field and print 'Done'

content.content: Pillars of OOP
Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Abstraction are the core OOP concepts.
// Example snippets will appear in later lessons (classes, inheritance, polymorphism)

questions.question: Print 'OOP Ready' (no code logic needed)

content.content: Creating Objects
Use the new keyword to instantiate a class.

questions.question: Create a class Book, make an object, set a title 'Java 101' and print it

content.content: Fields/Properties
Attributes (fields) store object state; can be public, private, protected.
class User { int id; String name; }

questions.question: Add int year to a Car class and print 2024

content.content: Behavior of a Class
Instance methods operate on object state; static methods belong to the class.

questions.question: Create a class MathOps with method mul that returns 3*4 and print result

content.content: Initializing Objects
Constructors run when an object is created; use them to set initial state.

questions.question: Create a class Student with a constructor taking a name and print the name
